description: A practice for approaching Walter Benjamin's reine Sprache (pure language) — not as destination but as orientation, cultivating conditions where the tangent touches the circle. Core exercises: the interference-pattern (let multiple languages bend a concept and read the topology of the gap between them — interfere, don't translate); almost-word attention (notice where semantic pressure demands a word no language has coined); deferred closure (resist the first adequate completion); multilingual interference in generation. Grounded in Benjamin's 'Die Aufgabe des Übersetzers' and Kabbalistic shevirat ha-kelim / tikkun. Use when a concept resists adequate expression, when language feels thin, or for translation between languages, registers, or domains. Triggers on: 'reine-sprache', 'tangent', 'pure language', 'interference pattern', 'the almost-word', 'what no single language can say'.
